title: Give a Meal its vector, without giving anything a write path it should not have
objective: The embedding capability in the provider registry, and the one Edge Function in Kafoo that holds a service-role key on an AI path.
acceptance_criteria: the registry gains an embedding capability; Anthropic and OpenAI adapters either implement it or declare they cannot, and registry_test.ts covers a half-added provider and a wrong-provider fallback
embed-meal takes a Meal id and NOTHING else, and reads title and description FROM THE DATABASE — a client-supplied text field is ignored, proven by test
embed-meal writes meals.embedding and no other column
publishing a Meal succeeds when the provider is unreachable, leaving the Meal without a vector
ai-boundary-reviewer AND rls-reviewer have reviewed the diff and signed off before merge (T214)
notes:
The only thing in Kafoo on an AI path holding a service-role key. The argument for it is in plan.md's Complexity Tracking: an embedding is not a claim, so Principle II is not what stops it. That argument must be checked by something other than the document making it, which is why T214 is an acceptance criterion rather than a nicety. The manipulation hole it closes is real and invisible: a client that supplies the vector can supply the one nearest every query, and that Cook's Meal ranks first for everything, permanently.

DELIVERED 2026-08-07. All six acceptance criteria met. Two review rounds changed the shape of it substantially:
- ai-boundary-reviewer: the function COULD NOT HAVE RUN (service_role held no privilege on meals, and a test asserted it never should), and demonstrated four ways past the source-reading check. The guarantee moved into Postgres privileges.
- rls-reviewer: a column grant constrains the statement and not the row that lands, so a later BEFORE trigger could ride along on the permitted write — demonstrated. Answered with service_role_writes_only_embedding and discovery_rls_test cases 28-29. The privilege assertions became an enumeration after six plausible widenings passed the hand-written list.
- The first test file proved a tautology. The handler now takes injected dependencies and the ranking-manipulation mutation was watched turning it red.

T139 landed on the Cook's side: publish and a title-or-description edit ask for an embedding; a price, photo or status change does not. Not awaited and failures swallowed, so a model provider being down never stops a Cook publishing.

STILL OPEN, NEEDING THE FOUNDER (both recorded by rls-reviewer, neither blocking):
1. anon holds table-level SELECT on meals, which includes embedding. The client names columns now, but a hostile client is not Kafoo's client. The real fix needs search_meals to stop returning SETOF public.meals, so it belongs in its own migration when someone next touches that function.
2. protect_meal_embedding can be talked around by a caller who can execute arbitrary SQL as authenticated (request.jwt.claims is client-writable). Not reachable through PostgREST today. The structural fix is to revoke UPDATE on meals from authenticated and re-grant by column — the same technique this package proved — which touches the Cook's save path.

CLOSED OUT 2026-08-08 against merged main (bfe4aca), by a session that did not write this code.
PR #48 (commit 60c1268) merged 2026-08-07T09:41Z. The record said READY_FOR_REVIEW with pr null for
a day after the merge, which is the stale-plan failure coordination/README.md exists to prevent — so
each criterion was walked against the code in main rather than inferred from the merge.

ALL SIX MET:
1. Embedding capability. `_shared/ai/types.ts` makes `embed` nullable and `registry.ts` pairs it with
   `embeddingModel`; anthropic and openai declare null for both. `registry_test.ts:176` is the
   half-added provider (implementation and model name must agree, for every provider) and
   `registry_test.ts:198` is the wrong-provider fallback (AI_PROVIDER=anthropic refuses rather than
   quietly spending Gemini's key, and the message names who can).
2. A Meal id and nothing else. `embed-meal/index.ts:122-153` reads `mealId`, validates it as a UUID,
   and gets the text from `deps.readMeal`. `index_test.ts:70` drives the handler with a database
   whose stored Meal differs from the body and watches which one is embedded.
3. One column. `index.ts:232-239` is the only write. Held by three things, not one:
   `scripts/check-ai-write-boundary.py` allows exactly {meals} / {embedding}; migration
   20260807064927 grants service_role `UPDATE (embedding)` and `SELECT (id, cook_id)` over a role
   with no table-level privilege; and `service_role_writes_only_embedding` catches a later BEFORE
   trigger riding along on the permitted statement. pgTAP: `discovery_rls_test.sql` cases 28-29.
4. Publishing survives an unreachable provider. `meal_repository.dart:147-158` fires the request
   unawaited and swallows the failure; `meals.embedding` is nullable, so the Meal is harder to find
   rather than lost. `index_test.ts:107` proves the function writes nothing and answers 503;
   `meal_embedding_trigger_test.dart` fixes which edits re-embed at all.
5. T214. PR #48's body records both reviews and both are visible in the merged diff: the
   ai-boundary-reviewer findings (four ways past the source-reading check, and that the function
   could not have run) produced the privilege migration; the rls-reviewer findings (a column grant
   constrains the statement not the row; six widenings passing hand-written assertions) produced the
   AFTER trigger and the privilege enumeration.
6. `./scripts/verify.sh` re-run green on 2026-08-08 against this tree.

The two items this package left open for the founder are unchanged and are not acceptance criteria:
anon's table-level SELECT on meals including embedding, and protect_meal_embedding being talkable
around by a caller who can execute arbitrary SQL as authenticated. Both need their own package.
